title: Vanilla-cinnamon chia pudding
summary: Chia seeds soaked overnight in coconut and almond milk until they set into a thick, spoonable pudding; dairy-free as written.
steps: Whisk the coconut milk, almond milk, erythritol, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Whisk in the chia seeds, wait 5 minutes, then whisk again to break up the clumps that form.
Divide among four jars, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Stir before serving and top each jar with a few raspberries.
tips: For a smooth, custard-like texture, blend the pudding after it has set.
It keeps 4 days in the fridge, so it is easy to make ahead for breakfasts.

origin.history: Chia is native to Mexico and Central America and was a major crop of Mesoamerica; Aztec records list it among the goods paid as tribute. It was eaten as a grain and stirred into drinks, as in the chia fresca still made today. The soaked, pudding-style dish is a modern invention that spread with health-food cooking in the 2000s.
